events.label: Russell new indexes live — reconstitution takes effect at open
events.note: Russell 2026 reconstitution takes effect at Monday June 29 open. NVDA is now the #1 constituent in the Russell 3000/1000 Growth; MU and AMD are 100% Growth; AAPL/AMZN/MSFT weightings shifted toward Value; SpaceX (SPCX) added to Russell 1000. The June 26 closing cross was a record $334.027B in 1.63 seconds — largest Nasdaq closing-cross liquidity event ever. RESULT: passive bid overwhelmed by active selling — NVDA (-1.64%), MU (-2.1%), AMD (-2.6%) all fell despite the Growth ETF reclassification. Reconstitution cleanup/index tracking error correction may create mild additional early-week activity. June 29 is also the start of quarter-end window dressing week and the week containing the NFP (July 2).

events.label: Quarter-end / month-end window dressing — Q2 2026 close
events.note: Q2 2026 close. SPX is at 7,354 entering the week — down 1.73% for the week of June 22-26 and 106 pts below the 7,460 regime floor. Institutional window dressing typically lifts large-cap names into Q2 close; in current regime (VIX 18.89, five consecutive Nasdaq losing sessions, reconstitution bid failed), watch for rotation toward value/defensive rather than Nasdaq recovery. Close above 7,400 = first constructive signal of the week. Close below 7,300 activates BEARISH escalation framework.

events.label: ISM Manufacturing Index (10:00 AM ET) — first Q3 economic read
events.note: June ISM Manufacturing official release — first Q3 data point. June flash PMI Manufacturing was 55.7 (49-month high per S&P Global). ISM above 57 = goldilocks for AI/semis heading into Q3 (strong demand, oil disinflation). ISM below 50 = first recessionary data point since the BofA rate-hike repricing — forces regime re-evaluation and likely breaks SPX through 7,300. Key early-Q3 positioning catalyst.

events.label: June Non-Farm Payrolls 8:30 AM ET — PULLED FORWARD (markets closed July 3)
events.note: June employment report pulled forward from July 3 to Thursday July 2 because markets are closed July 3 (Independence Day observed — July 4 falls on Saturday). Consensus: +172K NFP, 4.3% unemployment, +0.3% wages. THREE SCENARIOS: (1) STRONG (+200K+, wages +0.4%) = BofA three-hike framework (Sep/Oct/Dec 2026) locked in; DXY spikes; 30Y approaches 5.00% trigger; SPX gaps lower July 7 — STEP ASIDE escalates to BEARISH. (2) GOLDILOCKS (130-180K, wages +0.2%) = regime conditions stabilize; HOLD upgrade possible for first Q3 briefing; IWM/QQQ pair and TLT hedge both exit. (3) WEAK (<130K, wages flat) = recession fears emerge; Fed hike narrative collapses; TLT long pays off but growth tech faces 'bad news is bad news' further selling. Markets closed July 3 — NFP reaction prints into a 3-day weekend gap; positions cannot be hedged until July 7 open.

events.label: US Market Holiday — Independence Day observed (July 4 falls on Saturday)
events.note: US equity markets closed Friday July 3 as July 4, 2026 falls on a Saturday. 3-day weekend gap (July 3-6). The June NFP report prints Thursday July 2 — any repricing accumulates over the full 3-day gap before July 7 open. This is the most dangerous NFP weekend gap in 2026 H2 positioning calendar: use July 2 close as the last chance to hedge or reduce before the gap.

events.label: FOMC Minutes from June 17 meeting (est.) — first post-dot-plot-removal release
events.note: Minutes from the June 17 FOMC meeting (est. release ~3 weeks after meeting). This is the first FOMC at which Warsh removed the dot plot — minutes will reveal the internal rate debate and degree of committee division on the Sep/Oct/Dec 2026 hike sequence BofA is forecasting. Unanimous hawkish tone = BofA 3-hike forecast solidified. Any dissent or hike-pause language = dovish surprise and rate relief. Key input for Q3 positioning heading into the July 14 CPI print.

events.label: June CPI release (est.) — most important inflation data of the summer
events.note: June CPI is the next major inflation recalibration after May PCE (June 25). Oil has now reversed the Hormuz spike — Brent settled $71.99 on June 26 (below June 25 close), confirming the disinflation path is intact. June CPI captures the first month of Hormuz normalization at scale. If CPI falls to 3.5% or below, the BofA 3-hike framework weakens materially and the July 28 FOMC hike probability collapses. If CPI holds at 4.0%+, September hike is locked in. July 14 is the critical regime-reset date for H2 2026 positioning.

events.label: FOMC meeting (July 28-29) — rate hike on the table
events.note: Nine of 18 FOMC officials projected at least one 2026 rate hike at the June 17 meeting. BofA calls for three hikes (Sep/Oct/Dec). A 25-bps hike (3.50-3.75% → 3.75-4.00%) at this meeting is a non-trivial probability if June CPI disappoints. June CPI (~July 14) is the primary input. Rate hike = BEARISH regime confirmation. Micron's $50B Q4 guidance does not override a rate hike decision — AI capex is robust but higher rates still compress growth multiples.

events.label: Iran-US Islamabad Declaration 60-day deadline — Hormuz full reopening + sanctions relief
events.note: Deal operational from June 18 MOU signing; 60-day window expires August 13. Brent settled $71.99 on June 26 (fully reversing the June 26 drone-strike spike), confirming tanker traffic is accelerating through Hormuz despite the incident. Trump labeled the drone strike a 'foolish violation of our Ceasefire Agreement' — signaling the administration remains committed to the framework. If August 13 deadline met with full Hormuz clearance, WTI could extend to $65-67 — extend XLE short and exit TBT. Failure = oil spike reversal and energy re-rally; the oil-crash pace is ahead of schedule.

events.label: SPCX first earnings as a public company (approx.) — Starlink ARR + Starship cadence
events.note: First earnings print since the June 12 IPO. SPCX confirmed in Russell 1000 effective June 29. Capital structure: $75B IPO + $60B xAI acquisition + $20B bond offering = $155B in obligations. First earnings (Starlink subscriber/ARR growth, Starship launch cadence, cash burn rate) is the fundamental clearing event for re-entry. Two consecutive closes above $185 on above-average volume required before re-entry from current ~$153 range.

events.label: SPCX 180-day IPO lock-up expiry (approx.) — insider/early-investor float unlock
events.note: ~180 days after the June 12 debut, early investors and insiders can sell, materially expanding the ~4% public float. Lock-up expiries are a known supply overhang for hot IPOs; the $20B bond offering (June 22) already changed the capital structure risk profile — the lock-up expiry adds equity supply overhang on top. Exact date pending the prospectus's stated terms.

events.label: OpenAI IPO — target window shifts to H1 2027 after 2026 delay
events.note: OpenAI delayed its anticipated 2026 IPO to H1 2027 (announced June 26, 2026). SoftBank sold off -13% on the delay (SoftBank is a major pre-IPO investor). Microsoft and NVIDIA hold strategic stakes. The delay removes a near-term AI sentiment catalyst and adds uncertainty to AI infrastructure spending trajectories. Monitor for filing date announcement as a potential AI sentiment catalyst. Date is approximate placeholder for H1 2027 window.
